clue.text: In class this boy when ordered sat, the creep

indicators.note: once the letters are put in a new order they spell something else, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolboy sat down in class and turned out to be a sneak, a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ordered' rearranges SAT THE CREEP. 'the creep' looks like the definition, but it is part of the anagram; the definition is the opening 'In class this boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who curries favour with the person running the classroom is that adult's favourite, so he is the boy described.

clue.text: Filthy carpet may eventually appear excellent

definitions.meaning: a very dirty rug needs a lot of hitting before it comes clean, i.e. it will need much thrashing
an idiom for being so good that it is hard to surpass

explanation.surface: A grubby rug might, after enough work, come up looking splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: carpets were cleaned by hanging them up and hitting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to better is said, idiomatically, to need a lot of beating before anything outdoes it.

clue.text: Curfew fully obeyed with no extra charges?

definitions.meaning: when everyone is indoors by the deadline, they are every one inside
an inclusive price covers everything, with nothing added later

explanation.surface: A curfew observed by everyone, and no penalty fees to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclusive deal bundles every cost together; the other sense is simply everybody being home.

clue.text: Greek goddess accepting one of her characters as mistress

indicators.note: the goddess takes in the letter, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Hera, queen of the Greek gods
her = the Greek goddess's language; eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess taking on one of her own personae as a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her characters' are Greek letters, not roles in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A hetaera was a courtesan in ancient Greece, a kept companion of wealthy men.

clue.text: Run over me, stopping short as a favour

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the word ends one letter early, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: in crosswords 'me' is often the setter of the puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be driven over, with the driver halting before the end, as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter, cut short by 'stopping short' to SETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour can be a ribbon badge or knot of ribbon worn to show support, which is a rosette.

clue.text: Child's hero follows papa as a minister

indicators.note: the hero's name comes after the papa letter

parts.note: P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Jack Reacher is the hero of Lee Child's thriller novels

explanation.surface: A child idolises a father who serves as a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Child is the author Lee Child, not a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion delivers sermons, so is a preacher.

clue.text: Suggesting better clothes shouldn't be put on, being drunk

definitions.text: Suggesting better clothes shouldn't be put on
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase says one is worse for wearing something, so best clothes are better left off
an idiom for intoxicated or in a poor state

explanation.surface: Someone who has had too much drink is told not to put on their good outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone damaged or impaired, commonly by too much alcohol.

clue.text: Dessert's up: at last spoon out and get a move on

indicators.note: that letter is taken away from the reversed dessert
in a down entry, up means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a pudding is a dessert; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Pudding is served: finally, ladle it out and hurry along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PUDDING to GNIDDUP; 'out' removes N, the end of 'spoon', picked by 'at last'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddup (giddy-up) is the call to make a horse go faster, an urge to hurry.

clue.text: Mean to be wasting years? Not altogether

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone intends to fritter away years, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Mean to be' as the definition, but only 'Mean' substitutes for the adjective; 'to be' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of tight-fisted with money is a synonym of miserly.

clue.text: What makes page dirty? A sort of bonk-lit

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so its letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Racy fiction might be said to soil the pages it is printed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sort of' rearranges BONKLIT; 'dirty' tempts toward smut, but the stain is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge of spilt ink is what spoils a clean sheet of paper.

clue.text: Swedish scientist is retired tennis champion

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: Chris Evert, multiple Grand Slam winner

explanation.surface: A Swede in the lab turns out to be a former tennis star now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolf Sievert was a Swedish medical physicist; the unit of radiation dose is named after him.

clue.text: Wickedness accepted by rich man: time to sell up

indicators.note: the rich man takes the wickedness in, so it goes inside him

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the parable of Lazarus
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A wealthy man takes on vice and decides it is time to liquidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell off one's holdings in a company is to withdraw investment from it.

clue.text: No Tolkien character gets backing to sing

indicators.note: going backwards, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: orcs are creatures in Tolkien's Middle-earth

explanation.surface: No figure from Tolkien finds support for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: To croon is to sing softly and sentimentally.

clue.text: A comedy show about to drop pet cat

indicators.note: turned about, so what remains is read backwards
the named word falls out of the longer one

parts.note: The Muppet Show was a TV comedy show

explanation.surface: A comedy programme is about to abandon a domestic cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes the word pet, which in the surface looks like the cat's description; 'about' then reverses what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a large wild American cat.

clue.text: Secretive, after spilling cereals without paying attention

indicators.note: the secretive word comes after the jumbled letters
spilt cereal scatters, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive

explanation.surface: Someone sneaky has spilt breakfast cereal through inattention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges CEREALS to CARELES.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carelessly means doing it heedlessly, without due thought.

clue.text: Newton was to emerge to get into motion

indicators.note: set moving, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Newton was going to come out and get things moving, his laws of motion in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into motion' rearranges TO EMERGE; the definition ends in a verb, to be completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton was a mathematician who worked in geometry, so he was a geometer.

clue.text: Trick ref and get United flying — on a roll

parts.note: a sub is a sandwich made on a long bread roll

indicators.note: flying about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A cheat fools the referee and sends United soaring on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges REF GET U to TERFUGE; 'on a roll' means a winning streak in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A subterfuge is a deceitful ruse or stratagem used to get one's way.

clue.text: What operators wear in prison?

definitions.meaning: surgeons wear ..., the plain clothing of the operating theatre
Wormwood ..., often just the ..., is a London prison

explanation.surface: What do surgeons wear when working in a jail?
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a prison in west London, known as the Scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre staff wear loose cotton garments; the other sense names a well-known British jail.

clue.text: University department failing to employ Conservative

indicators.note: the defective word takes on, i.e. holds, the Conservative inside it

parts.note: faulty means failing or defective

explanation.surface: A university department is failing because it refuses to hire a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a grouping of related academic subjects in a university.

clue.text: Festival — it lifted a Roman province

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means written upwards, i.e. reversed

explanation.surface: A festival raised spirits in a province of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatia was a region of central Anatolia organised as a province of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Buffoons lowering the odds of seeing these?

definitions.text: Buffoons lowering the odds of seeing these?

indicators.note: take down the odd letters, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: Clowns make it less likely that we will spot flying saucers.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters (first, third, fifth, seventh) of 'Buffoons' and the evens remain; the whole clue also hints at the sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are what people claim to see in the sky; fools make the claims less credible.

clue.text: Turn cross, receiving hard riddle from one

indicators.note: the turning word takes in the hard letter

parts.note: to spin is to turn
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: Someone turns angry when handed a tough puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is not angry but the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sphinx of Thebes posed a famous riddle to travellers, so a riddle comes from this creature.

clue.text: Inserting end of chisel, make bigger hole in sphere

indicators.note: that letter goes into the boring word

parts.note: to ream is to enlarge a bored hole

indicators.note: only the last letter of chisel is used

explanation.surface: A craftsman uses a chisel to widen a hole in a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field of activity, as is a sphere.

clue.text: Evoke birdsong, not one of the top three we hear

parts.note: a call is a bird's cry

indicators.note: the placing is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: not one of the top three
parts.note: fourth place is just outside the medals

explanation.surface: A bird's song that recalls coming just off the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up or elicit, a synonym for drawing something out.

clue.text: Establish there's nothing in cash

indicators.note: the nothing letter sits in the cash word

parts.note: a fund is a store of money
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Setting up a business when there is no money in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up for the first time.

clue.text: Port and cheese nicked, neither finished

indicators.note: both words lose their final letter

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Fortified wine and cheese were stolen, both partly consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither finished' strips the final E of BRIE and of STOLE. 'Port' looks like the wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a city in south-west England with a long history as a seaport.

clue.text: May baby's nature appear at first unusual?

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: made unusual, so the letters are rearranged
only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Is the temperament of a child born in May odd from the start?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges NATURE with A, the first letter of 'appear'.
explanation.definitionFit: People born from late April to late May fall under the star sign Taurus, the bull.

clue.text: Unequally carve up goose, madly merry tucking in

indicators.note: the goose takes the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: a gander is a male goose

indicators.note: madly suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A carver hacks the Christmas goose into uneven portions while cheerfully eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' marks the anagram and 'tucking in' the insertion; in the surface 'tucking in' means eating heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral boundaries are rigged when districts are drawn unfairly to favour one party.
